fit: inherited folate disorder and acute combined-treatment drooling
assessment: The complete original on pp. 921–922 documents baseline drooling and an acute crisis after combined treatment. No graded change or raw fig exposure was measured.

fit: test bolus texture and airway protection in Parkinson and stroke populations
assessment: A referred clinical series analyzes 844 swallows in 110 people. The swallow safety comparison uses standardized textures with no fig exposure or drooling severity outcome.

fit: drooling ratings and paraffin-stimulated salivary flow
assessment: Table 1 records median Sialorrhea Clinical Scale scores 1.5 versus 0 and stimulated flow 1.6 versus 6 mL/min. These contrasting measures describe a cross-sectional difference without dietary attribution.
The original abstract confirms distinct saliva, swallow and drooling assessments. The full comparative results remain open and the authors tested no fig exposure.

fit: observed drooling frequency and severity under divided attention
assessment: The registry and earlier MDS abstract describe the same 18-person results family. Distraction reduced swallowing frequency and increased drooling frequency. Severity did not clearly differ and no food was tested.

fit: wrist cueing and perceived drooling severity
assessment: The immediate versus delayed comparison reports a diary severity difference, with less conclusive ROMP–Saliva and UPDRS results. The 28-person pooled analysis reuses the same intervention participants. The study has no food exposure.

fit: rehabilitation, pooled saliva and perceived drooling
assessment: The ten completers had less endoscopic vallecular saliva residue after rehabilitation. Their ROMP–Saliva change was inconclusive. No food treatment or raw fig comparison was assigned.
